messages.subject: NA in marker data
messages.body_plain:
Dear  simplePHENOTYPES developers,
I am trying to use simplePHENOTYPES for phenotype simulation.
I have genotyped RIL population, but because it is real data some of markers include missing values (as "NA").
I used code of first example  and got error "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"

df_t_na <- read.csv("mxc_na.csv")
create_phenotypes(
  geno_obj = df_t_na,
  add_QTN_num = 3,
  add_effect = 0.2,
  big_add_QTN_effect = 0.9,
  rep = 10,
  h2 = 0.7,
  model = "A",
  na_string = "NA",
  home_dir = getwd())
When I changed "NA" to "0" as Aa it works fine.
Could you please help me to solve this problem?
I attached file with genotyping.

Thank you very much in advance!

messages.subject: Re: NA in marker data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Andrii Fatiukha,
This is a small bug that I need to fix. In summary, simplePHENOTYPES does not accept missing data.
It will do an imputation when converting from HapMap (or another format) to numeric. But since your data is already numeric, it doesn't go through the numericalization/imputation step.

I will fix it as soon as possible, thanks for letting me know.

Meanwhile, here is a quick fix for you. With the code below you can impute your data by setting missing genotypes as heterozygotes, or as the most frequent genotype. For purpose of simulation, it doesn't make much difference. The simulation code below should work fine after this imputation.

Cheers,
Samuel

# missing data imputation
# missing will be set as hets
df_t_na[is.na <http://is.na>(df_t_na)] <- 0

# missing will be set as the most frequent
d2 <-t(apply(df_t_na[,-1:-5], 1, function(x){
  tab <- table(unlist(x))
  x[is.na <http://is.na>(x)] <- as.numeric(names(tab[which.max(tab)]))
  return(x)
}))
df_t_na <- data.frame(df_t_na[,1:5], d2)

create_phenotypes(
  geno_obj = df_t_na,
  add_QTN_num = 3,
  add_effect = 0.2,
  big_add_QTN_effect = 0.9,
  rep = 10,
  h2 = 0.7,
  model = "A",
  na_string = "NA",
  home_dir = getwd())
